newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., to release plan to aid Miami.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., to release plan to aid Miami.

text.p: Dade County, Fla., Mayor Alex Penelas said he would release a plan Thursday outlining steps the county could take to help ease Miami's fiscal crisis.
Penelas set a news conference for 11 a.m. EST to outline his proposals, which could include buying city properties and extending a small line of credit.
Penelas said he would also urge the county to draft a contingency plan on how it could provide services to Miami "in case the city is abolished or goes bankrupt."

Miami, the county seat, has a $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget for the year that began Oct 1. Gov. Lawton Chiles said he would appoint an oversight board by the end of next week to advise the city, although it will not have authority to overrule the city commission.

City officials said filing for bankruptcy would be premature and is not currently an option. Disgruntled residents have proposed dissolving the city and absorbing it into the county government, and have collected enough voter signatures to force a referendum on the proposal.
